sections.text: The inhabitants of the world, misled by those natures which the Qualities have engendered, know not that I am higher than them all, and that I do not change.
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया।
Verily, this Divine Illusion of Phenomenon manifesting itself in the Qualities is difficult to surmount. Only they who devote themselves to Me and to Me alone can accomplish it.
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः।
The sinner, the ignorant, the vile, deprived of spiritual perception by the glamour of Illusion, and he who pursues a godless life - none of them shall find Me.

We are discussing Chapter 7, Gnana Vignana Yoga, the Yoga of Knowledge and Wisdom. In this chapter we have seen that the Lord says, You complain that you dont know the Lord, that you have never seen God before. But I pervade this universe with my Ashta Dha Prakriti. In my Eightfold nature, I manifest in this world, and you see me every day.
That is Bhumiyapo anala kam vayuhu Manabuddhi Ahankar. Thats my Eightfold Prakriti. And you see me every day.
This is my lower Prakriti. Lower means the grosser manifestation which you and I can perceive through our senses. But he said, higher than that is my higher Prakriti, which is not just the sum total of all this, but something which is the cause for this entire universe.
Everything comes out of me and everything goes back into me. It stays in time and space in a particular shape or form or state temporarily, but eventually it goes back to its source, which is the self -- the self which is all-pervading. Therefore there is nothing other than myself.
Anything which you can see is nothing but myself. Therefore all the examples then given show that whatever you see is me. In the last verse, in the previous three verses we have seen, it says Ye chaiva Sattvika Bhava Rajasas Tamasash cha ye.
Matta eveti tan viddhi na tv aham teshu te mayi. This world right now seems divided into three types of people, three types of things, three types of qualities. These are the qualities of my Maya.
This illusion creates a world of plurality when only one exists -- the singularity -- and it does so by fooling my mind and intellect. I see this plurality. And I say that this illusion which I see is because of the divine Prakriti called Maya.
This Maya has three aspects: Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. Sattva is pure knowledge or existence. Rajas is activity.
And Tamas is inertia. These three are absolutely required for anything to exist. The awareness that it exists, the activity, dynamism, and then inertia -- all three in different proportions, in different permutation and combination, create this world of plurality.
So any being you see in this world -- whether Sattvik, Rajasik, or Tamasic -- they come from me, they are in me, but I am not in them. Now obviously, our whole life weve heard that Bhagavan is in every being. But now Bhagavan says they are in me, but I am not in them.
When we discussed this verse, we used a simple analogy: the universal space says, Im not in the car, but the car is in me. A car is traveling in space. The space inside the car -- is it in the car, or is it remaining where it is? The car is traveling in the space. We feel the space in the car; otherwise we wouldnt be able to sit in it.
However, when the car moves from Hanover County to Henrico, it doesnt carry the Hanover County space to Henrico. Otherwise Henrico would have a surplus of space. The space remains where it is.
Even though in my perception it seems like the space is in the car, in reality the car is in the space. So even though it seems like Bhagavan is in me -- thats why I can speak, I can hear, I can walk -- actually I am in the Lord. As long as I keep connected with Him, I can do all of that.
So the next three verses. Verse 13: Mohitam na abhijanati mam ebhyah param avyayam. All this elaborate explanation creates a confusion in our mind: So if thats the case, why dont I feel the Lords presence? All this is great, but I dont feel it. Because Bhagavan says this world is deluded by the three qualities of Maya -- Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas -- which create this magnificent projection of the world.
We go to a cinema theater; we know its just a screen and light is thrown on it. But we get caught up in the images, the storyline, and the acting. We forget completely that whats in front of us is nothing but a white screen with light projected through a lens -- that magnificent projection.
So its even more confusing for us: what is real and what is unreal? Up till now, at least with the 2D world, we could say, Thats two-dimensional. My world is three-dimensional. Many years ago I went to Epcot Center, and that was the first time Id seen a hologram. I was completely baffled.
The lady looked so real in the hologram, walking around giving a presentation. Luckily it was not full scale, so you could tell. But its so real that our senses cannot differentiate between what is real and what is unreal.
Same thing with Photoshop. Previously, when somebody sent me a picture, I knew what it was. Now somebody sends me a picture and I dont know whether its Photoshopped or real.
Im in a party, but I was never there -- because somebody photoshopped me into it. The more the world creates these magnificent projections, the more we get deluded. The more our senses are involved, the more it confuses us from differentiating the real from the unreal.
So Bhagavan said that these three qualities of His Prakriti, projected through His Prakriti -- His Prakritis nature is this divine Maya, the divine illusion which creates multiple entities out of one. This world is deluded by this -- Mam na abhijanati mam ebhyah param avyayam -- and therefore they do not know that I am the immutable source of all beings. It is as simple as this: Bhagavan said, Its me.
I created the confusion in your mind. I am the source of the confusion. So we say, Well then, why are we suffering? Bhagavan, why didnt you create a simple world where everybody understands that we are part of the Lord? But in fact, we dont like simple things. The more confusing it is -- thats why we want 3D TV now.
Up till now, we were happy with 2D TV. The more baffling it is, the more interesting. A magic trick that somebody can figure out is no longer magic -- I dont want to go see it.
But something I cant figure out? How does David Copperfield make the Statue of Liberty vanish? The whole United States tunes into the television set. More confusing, more interesting. Thats what makes our life interesting.
Bhagwan said, Thats what my Leela is. We get caught in the play; we lose the sense of what is real and what is unreal. So the next verse: Daivi hi esha gunamayi mama maya duratyaya. This divine Maya of mine -- Maya is divine because, after all, it is the Lords quality.
He says, This is my quality. But it is very difficult to overcome. We know that when we go to see a magic show, almost 100% of the people in the audience know there is no real magic. He is not cutting this lady in half.
But at the same token, we cant figure out how he did it. We actually had a magic show at Chinmaya Mission -- probably you may have seen this. It was a fundraiser, and they had all these acts.
One act was: they put, Dheerananda, into this box and rotated the box around. When you opened it, the He was gone and a young little kid in a monastic dress came out. Oh, what did you do? You made a little kid! Unfortunately, there were obviously two compartments and the guy switches around. But s saffron robe got stuck in the partition.
So when the little kid comes out, we see the saffron robe, and the whole magic is gone. Everybodys laughing. We figured out It is right behind that curtain.
This magic is only enjoyable as long as we cant figure it out. Once we figure it out, the magic is gone. Bhagavan says, I am the greatest magician, so you cant figure out my Maya. This threefold Maya of mine is difficult to overcome.
With a simple mind and intellect, youre trying to figure out the Lords Maya -- your mind and intellect are not capable. Bhagavan says, you can try all your life, generations after generations, to intellectually figure out the Lords nature. Youre not going to succeed.
Bhagawan says, Mama Maya Duratyaya -- it is very difficult to cross over. But then we say, Okay, thats the end of this class. Lets close the book.
Lets go home. Mam eva ye prapadyante mayam etam taranti te. Those who take refuge in me will cross over. This Maya, we are all very anxious to find out.
Well, the magician says, if you come and take, become my disciple, then you will figure out everything what I do. So when you go to the source and take refuge in him, if I really want to find out what David Copperfield does, I have to go and bow down and say, take me as your disciple. Let me know how you make this statue of Liberty vanishes.
Thats the purpose of my life. Okay, then Ill teach you. Bhagavan says, Mama Maya Duratyaya -- its very difficult to cross over if you just rely on your own intellect and mind.
But if you take refuge in me -- in other words, start identifying with the self -- you will overcome that. Thats the little escape hatch you have. Mam eva ye -- those who invoke me, or Bhajanti.
Now, we basically think about singing Bhajans, like Dheerananda. Its not just the harmonium and tabla. Bhajanti means: anytime we have to do something, we have to invoke ourselves.
When somebody asks me, Rajan, how did you do this? -- I did it all by myself. I had to invoke myself to do it. For something else you might say, Well, no, I had a little help from this organization, but I still did it myself. So I invoked the organization for some help, but I still myself is doing it. But she did it herself or something else.
Well, they didnt do it, but he did it himself. Wherever there is something doing comes, there is some self involved in it. Whether it is myself, yourself, herself, themselves, itself, the self involved in it.
In other words, in any activity you have to invoke self. That self is the doer, whether it is myself or yourself or herself or himself. The self is the only doer.
If there is no self involved, nothing happens. So we have to invoke the self. Now, the question is: with what instrument do we invoke it? To get the light in this room, I have to invoke electricity.
So I have to flip the switch, connect that to all the lights here and the lights come on.

The entire world is deluded by the three qualities (gunas) and does not recognize Me, who am beyond them and imperishable. This verse explains why spiritual realization seems so elusive. Like watching a captivating movie, we become so absorbed in the play of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas that we forget we are the witness, not the movie. Today, notice how your moods shift throughout the day: clarity and peace (sattva), restlessness and ambition (rajas), heaviness and confusion (tamas). Can you observe these shifting states without being completely identified with them?
Krishna offers both a warning and a promise. The warning: This divine Maya of Mine, consisting of the three gunas, is difficult to cross. The promise: Those who take refuge in Me alone shall cross over this illusion. The key word is alone (eva). Half-hearted seeking, divided attention, keeping one foot in spiritual practice and both hands grasping worldly security, this approach will not work. The magicians tricks cannot be understood from the audience; you must become his disciple. Today, honestly assess: how much of your day is spent genuinely seeking truth versus being entertained by the magic show of Maya?
The verse about those who do not seek the Divine describes them as deprived of spiritual perception by the glamour of Illusion. This is not a judgment but a diagnosis. The cure is Bhajanti, which means invoking the Self. Every action requires invoking some self: myself, yourself, itself. Today, consciously invoke the higher Self before important activities. Before a meeting, a difficult conversation, or creative work, pause and remember: May the Divine intelligence work through me.
